scored.title: Electrocardiogram-Based Deep Learning to Prioritize Testing for Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
scored.why: This diagnostic test study developed and validated a deep learning model reading electrocardiogram (ECG) images to flag transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.84 internally and 0.78-0.89 across five external multinational cohorts, plus three prospective screening cohorts, with sequential AI-ECG plus AI-echocardiography raising positive predictive value from 0.24 to 0.66. The scale of external and prospective screening validation, and the local deployability from routine ECG images rather than raw signals, make this a strong example of AI moving toward real-world case-finding for an underdiagnosed, treatable disease.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Acquisition and Interpretation for Screening Aortic Stenosis.
scored.why: This diagnostic study developed a deep learning algorithm for detecting moderate or greater aortic stenosis (AS) from AI-guided focused cardiac ultrasound (FoCUS), then prospectively tested it with novice operators across multiple Mayo Clinic sites, achieving 93% sensitivity and 96% specificity with 96.6% of scans usable, and expert review raising positive predictive value from 49.4% to 91.1%. The prospective, multi-site validation with non-expert operators demonstrates a real path toward decentralized valve disease screening, a genuine capability advance beyond retrospective algorithm development.

scored.title: Toward unified and comprehensive automated electroencephalogram interpretation: a multicentre development and validation of an electroencephalogram foundation model.
scored.why: This multicentre study developed a foundation model for electroencephalogram (EEG) interpretation trained on 18,677 patients and externally validated on 1573 patients across 48 institutions, achieving area under the curve (AUC) scores of 0.86-0.98 across 17 findings and matching or exceeding expert consensus on inter-rater reliability (IRR) analysis. The breadth of tasks covered, the scale of external validation across nearly 50 institutions, and the direct comparison to human expert agreement make this a substantial step toward deployable general-purpose EEG interpretation rather than another narrow single-task model.

scored.title: Machine Learning-Driven Risk Prediction Model in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
scored.why: This multicenter cohort study built a random survival forest machine learning (ML) model predicting mortality and heart failure hospitalization in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), validated via internal-external cross-validation across three European cohorts (n=850), with Harrell concordance indices of 0.72-0.77, outperforming existing Mayo and National Amyloidosis Centre staging systems by 2-19% depending on metric. The rigorous held-out validation across centers strengthens confidence in generalizability, though the improvement over existing staging systems, while real, is incremental rather than transformative.

scored.title: Multimodal artificial intelligence-based long-term mortality prediction after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a multicentre development, validation, and testing study.
scored.why: This multicentre study developed multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) models integrating clinical, imaging, and procedural data to predict long-term mortality after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in 3991 patients from Switzerland and Japan, with external testing at the second center and comparison against established surgical risk scores like the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS-PROM). The multimodal data integration and true geographic external validation against clinical standard-of-care risk scores represents a methodologically solid advance, though as with most survival prediction models the incremental benefit over existing scores needs confirmation in more diverse populations.

scored.title: Non-inferiority analysis of a fetal heart rate artificial intelligence algorithm to registered nurse assessment.
scored.why: This retrospective non-inferiority study compared an artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm's labeling of cardiotocography (CTG) fetal heart rate and uterine activity data against registered nurse (RN) readers across 800 tracings from five US hospitals, finding the algorithm met the 15% non-inferiority threshold for most endpoints except contraction duration. This is a genuine head-to-head comparison against real clinical staff on a common obstetric monitoring task, though the retrospective design and single comparator group (RNs rather than physicians) limit how strongly it supports full clinical deployment.

scored.title: Machine Learning-Based First-Trimester Antenatal Risk Prediction for Adverse Maternal and Neonatal Outcomes: Multicenter Model Development Study.
scored.why: This multicenter model development study trained separate machine learning models (LightGBM, light gradient boosting machine) on first-trimester data from over 700,000 pregnancies across Sweden, Chile, and Singapore, showing improved discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, of 0.60 to 0.65) over existing guideline- or clinician-based risk assessment (AUROC 0.52 to 0.56) for a composite adverse maternal and neonatal outcome. The large multinational scale and direct comparison against real-world clinical practice make this one of the stronger obstetric risk prediction studies this cycle, though the absolute discrimination remains modest and only internally validated within each country's own data.

scored.title: Detecting Incisional Surgical Site Infections on Wound Images Through Deep Learning.
scored.why: This diagnostic study trained a convolutional neural network on 4978 wound images to detect surgical site infections (SSI) and externally validated it on 407 prospectively collected images, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.91 internally and 0.82 externally with a positive decision curve analysis. The external validation and prospective image collection are genuine strengths for a telemedicine triage tool, though the external dataset is modest in size and single-center, limiting confidence in broader generalizability.

scored.title: Large Language Models as a New Tool for Therapists in Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy: Blinded Clinician Rating Pilot Experiment.
scored.why: In a preregistered blinded clinician rating experiment, 54 raters compared human versus large language model (LLM)-generated therapist responses within a simulated internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy (iCBT) protocol, finding statistically similar quality across dimensions (overall quality d=0.06, empathy d=0.42) and that raters correctly identified human responses more often (79%) than LLM ones (63%). This is a genuine blinded comparison against real clinician output with a preregistered design, which is the kind of evidence this beat should prioritize, though the patient messages were fictitious rather than real clinical cases.

scored.title: Physician-revised AI-generated drafts are associated with higher ratings of written explanations in end-of-life care in the intensive care unit: a scenario-based single-center cross-sectional study.
scored.why: In a scenario-based cross-sectional study with 45 raters, physician-revised drafts of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated responses to simulated intensive care unit (ICU) end-of-life questions received significantly higher ratings for medical validity and empathy than either physician-only or AI-only responses, with the empathy gain being more pronounced. This directly tests a collaborative human-AI workflow against both pure-human and pure-AI output on a high-stakes communication task, which is more informative than typical rubric-only studies, though it is single-center and scenario-based rather than drawn from real patient encounters.

scored.title: Predictive Models of Pregnancy Based on Male Partner Data From a Preconception Cohort Study.
scored.why: This prospective preconception cohort study used machine learning (ML) on 185 male partner variables from 2843 couples to predict spontaneous conception, with the best logistic regression models achieving area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) around 0.64-0.65, modestly better than chance but far from strong discrimination. The large, well-characterized prospective cohort and novel focus on male-partner predictors are notable strengths, though the modest predictive performance limits immediate clinical applicability.

scored.title: Expert Fusion Network for Automated Blastocyst Morphology and IVF Decision Support.
scored.why: This study developed the Expert Fusion Network (EFN), a mixture-of-experts deep learning architecture with a U-Net segmentation backbone, to classify and segment trophectoderm, blastocoel, and inner cell mass in blastocyst images, achieving F1-scores of 0.90 to 0.97 and Dice similarity coefficients around 0.90 to 0.92 with cross-dataset generalization on an independent set of 2,344 annotated images. The cross-dataset testing is a meaningful step beyond typical single-center embryo grading models, but the authors themselves note prospective clinical validation against IVF outcomes is still needed before this can inform embryo selection decisions.

scored.title: Automating the Management of Extraspinal Findings in Magnetic Resonance Imaging Spine Studies Using a Privacy-Preserving Large Language Model: Retrospective Validation Study.
scored.why: In this retrospective validation study, a privacy-preserving large language model (PP-LLM) automatically detected extraspinal findings on 400 spine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reports, correctly identifying 99.8% of findings and all clinically urgent cases, with 96.3% accuracy on specialty referral decisions and near-perfect agreement (Gwet's kappa 0.959) with clinician review. This is a solid general clinical AI workflow application with strong numbers on a modest single-center retrospective sample, but it has no reproductive focus beyond gynecologic findings being one incidental category and needs prospective, multi-site testing before workflow deployment.

scored.title: NICE: A Two-Step Non-Invasive Framework for Embryo cfDNA Read Enrichment and Quality Assessment.
scored.why: This study introduced NICE, a two-step framework combining an improved cell-free DNA (cfDNA) purification algorithm (DECENT-plus) with machine learning classifiers to reduce maternal DNA contamination in non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing (niPGT) from spent embryo culture medium, aiming to improve embryo ploidy assessment and quality classification. The technical contribution addresses a known contamination problem that limits clinical adoption of niPGT, but the abstract reports no external clinical outcome data such as implantation or live birth rates tied to the framework's classifications.

scored.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Endodontic Irrigants: A Structured Assessment of Accuracy, Readability, Hallucination Subtypes and Clinical Risk.
scored.why: This study systematically evaluated four large language models (LLMs), ChatGPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, and DeepSeek 3.2, on 100 endodontic irrigation questions each, scoring accuracy, hallucination subtype, clinical risk, and ten-day test-retest stability, finding DeepSeek had the highest hallucination rate (29%) and 16% critical-risk outputs while hallucination strongly correlated with clinical risk (rho 0.93). The hallucination-subtyping and temporal stability analysis is a more rigorous failure-mode characterization than typical single-snapshot rubric scoring, though it still lacks a comparison against real clinician answers to patients.

scored.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Antepartum Depression Symptoms: A Prospective Cohort Study.
scored.why: This prospective cohort study of 1701 pregnant women used several machine learning (ML) algorithms with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) feature selection to predict antepartum depression, with the best models achieving area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) around 0.71-0.76 but low precision (23-58%) and inconsistent sensitivity, particularly poor for the extreme gradient boosting model at 15.7% sensitivity. The prospective design is a modest strength, but the modest and inconsistent discrimination across algorithms with no external validation limits its immediate clinical utility.

scored.title: Eliminating Registration Bias in Synthetic CT Generation using a physics-based simulation framework for pelvic anatomy.
scored.why: This technical study proposed a physics-based simulation framework to generate geometrically aligned training pairs for synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generation from cone-beam CT (CBCT) in pelvic anatomy, showing improved geometric alignment metrics and downstream segmentation performance (Dice similarity coefficient, DSC, up to 0.92) compared to real-paired training data. This is a solid methods contribution to image synthesis for radiotherapy planning with a gynecological dataset component, but it is an engineering validation study without a direct patient outcome or reproductive-specific clinical question.

scored.title: MicrotiaGPT: Appraisal of Microtia Care Recommendations From an Artificially Intelligent Chatbot.
scored.why: This study had 23 pediatric otolaryngologists and audiologists rate ChatGPT-4o responses to standardized microtia and aural atresia questions on accuracy, comprehensiveness, and similarity to physician responses, finding generally high ratings but a reading level exceeding recommended patient education standards and gaps in empathetic framing. It goes slightly beyond typical rubric-only chatbot evaluations by comparing responses to real physician answers and surfacing a specific failure mode around parental guilt and terminology, which gives it modest value for this reader's beat.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence Chatbots and Large Language Models for Traumatic Dental Injury Management and Decision Support: A Systematic Review With Function-Based Narrative Synthesis and Exploratory Meta-Analysis.
scored.why: This systematic review with function-based narrative synthesis and exploratory meta-analysis pooled 28 studies on artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots and large language models (LLMs) in traumatic dental injury management, finding a pooled 81.7% rate of accurate or guideline-concordant responses across nine comparable studies, though with very high heterogeneity. It synthesizes existing rubric-style evidence rather than adding a new clinician comparator or deployment, but its scale and structured categorization of translational functions make it a useful field-level reference.

scored.title: Quality and reliability of YouTube videos on PET/CT radiation safety: a comparative analysis between human experts and large language models.
scored.why: This study compared a human nuclear medicine physician's rating of YouTube video quality on PET/CT (positron emission tomography/computed tomography) radiation safety against an AI model (Gemini-3) acting as an automated moderator, finding only slight agreement (Cohen's Kappa=0.191) and that the AI systematically overrated commercially biased content while penalizing technical academic videos. This reveals a concrete failure mode of using an LLM as a content moderation substitute for physician judgment, which is more informative than a typical rubric-only chatbot study, though it is a single-rater, single-topic comparison.

scored.title: Ensuring trustworthy AI assisted guideline development for clinical practice.
scored.why: This is a commentary responding to another paper's agentic large language model (LLM) system for drafting clinical guidelines, proposing safeguards like calibrated deferral and human validation rather than presenting new empirical results. As opinion and critique rather than a study with data, it offers limited actionable evidence for this reader despite touching on legitimate concerns about LLM-based evidence synthesis.

scored.title: The Quantification Paradox in Gynecologic Color Doppler Ultrasound: From Spectral Indices to Microvascular Imaging and Artificial Intelligence.
scored.why: This is a narrative review reorganizing the literature on gynecologic color Doppler ultrasound around measurement reproducibility rather than disease category, discussing emerging tools like superb microvascular imaging, contrast-enhanced ultrasound, radiomics, and deep learning without presenting new primary data. While it makes a reasonable methodological argument about prioritizing standardization over chasing another high area under the curve (AUC) biomarker, as a review it does not offer a new finding to act on.

scored.title: Information-driven nanozyme screening enabled sensitive detection of seminal neutral α-glucosidase activity reveals clinical infertility relevance.
scored.why: This study developed a nanozyme-based colorimetric biosensor for detecting seminal neutral alpha-glucosidase (NAG) activity as a marker of epididymal function, using machine learning only to screen candidate catalytic materials and a large language model (LLM) for literature-based synthesis route generation. The clinical correlation with male fertility status is a real but modest finding, and the AI components here are auxiliary tools in a chemistry and biosensing pipeline rather than a clinical decision-making system.

scored.title: Development and internal validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting vancomycin-induced nephrotoxicity in hospitalized children.
scored.why: This retrospective, single-center study developed an XGBoost model using electronic health record (EHR) data from 1,452 pediatric patients to predict vancomycin-induced nephrotoxicity, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.90 with a simplified six-feature version performing comparably. It is methodologically careful with SHAP interpretability and decision curve analysis but is internally validated only at one hospital, has no reproductive relevance, and adds to an already crowded space of single-center pediatric nephrotoxicity prediction models.

scored.title: Quality, transparency, and readability of AI chatbot responses for patient counseling in robot-assisted colorectal cancer resection: a cross-sectional evaluation.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study had raters score four chatbots' answers to 30 patient questions about robot-assisted colorectal cancer resection using the DISCERN quality instrument and Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT), finding ChatGPT scored highest but transparency about sources was uniformly poor across all models and readability exceeded recommended levels. This is a routine rubric-based chatbot evaluation without any clinician comparator or patient outcome measure, so it adds incremental rather than field-changing information.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence Answering Patient Questions About Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip: Accuracy, Readability, and Clinical Utility.
scored.why: This study had five pediatric orthopedic surgeons rate a Department of Defense-approved chatbot's answers to 12 questions about developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), finding all responses rated satisfactory or excellent but with poor single-rater reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient, ICC, of 0.12) that improved only to moderate agreement when averaged across raters. This is a small, rubric-based accuracy check without a clinician-answer comparator, and the weak inter-rater reliability undercuts confidence in the reported quality ratings.

scored.title: Guideline-based evaluation of large language models for patient counselling before robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: accuracy, safety, and readability.
scored.why: Blinded urologists rated five large language models (LLMs) answering 20 questions about robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) using multiple standardized instruments, finding ChatGPT scored highest on factual accuracy (89.4%) and quality metrics though not significantly different from DeepSeek after correction, and all models exceeded recommended reading levels. This is another rubric-based multi-model comparison without a human-clinician-generated comparator, which is routine for this beat despite the rigor of using several validated instruments.

scored.title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study.
scored.why: Researchers developed a diabetes-specialized large language model (LLM) using reflection- and curriculum-based instruction tuning, showing a 59.03% relative improvement over a zero-shot baseline on diabetes benchmarks and a modest 0.66% gain in a dietary quality index versus GPT-4, with simulation-based glycemic testing showing reduced postprandial glucose burden. This is primarily a model-development and benchmark study rather than a test against real clinicians or real patient interactions, limiting its relevance to this beat's focus on clinician comparison or deployment.

scored.title: The consent gap in ambient clinical artificial intelligence: what patients are not being told.
scored.why: No abstract text is provided beyond the title, which concerns disclosure practices around ambient clinical artificial intelligence (AI) tools that passively record patient encounters; this appears to be a commentary or opinion piece rather than an empirical study. Without any data or methodology to evaluate, this cannot be scored as a substantive research contribution.

scored.title: Induced pluripotent stem cells from discovery to translation.
scored.why: This is a narrative review discussing the translational trajectory of induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technology from discovery to clinical application, mentioning AI and automation only as a forward-looking consideration for scaling manufacturing workflows. There is no primary data, algorithm, or clinical evaluation here, and the core subject matter, stem cell biology, sits outside the AI-in-medicine beats this digest covers.

scored.title: Reply to ensuring trustworthy AI assisted guideline development for clinical practice.
scored.why: This is a reply to a Matters Arising commentary defending the design choices of an agentic large language model (LLM) system called Quicker for drafting clinical practice guidelines, with no new empirical data presented. It is purely an editorial exchange about governance and trust in AI-assisted evidence synthesis, offering little new information for this reader beyond the original debate.

scored.title: When machines misread science: creating guardrails for human and AI interpretation of biomedical research.
scored.why: This is a perspective piece arguing that biomedical science reporting standards should be modernized to prevent both human and artificial intelligence (AI) misinterpretation of research findings, without presenting new empirical data or a specific evaluated intervention. It raises a valid conceptual concern about AI as a science interpreter but offers no study design, metric, or result for this reader to act on.

scored.title: Prenatal urinary phenanthrene metabolites associated with fetal growth restriction: a nested case-control study with integrated computational toxicology.
scored.why: This nested case-control study within a prospective birth cohort examined maternal urinary polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) metabolites in relation to fetal growth restriction (FGR), using conditional logistic regression with machine learning primarily as a variable prioritization step, followed by network toxicology and in vitro trophoblast experiments. The core contribution is environmental toxicology and mechanistic biology rather than a clinical AI system, so despite competent design it falls outside this digest's AI-focused beats.

scored.title: Automated luteal blood perfusion assessment in cows using image processing and deep learning algorithms.
scored.why: This study compared human evaluation, pixel-counting software, and a deep learning (DL) pipeline for estimating luteal blood perfusion in cattle from color Doppler ultrasound, finding positive correlations among the three methods (r greater than or equal to 0.52) and biological validity against progesterone levels. This is a veterinary reproductive physiology study with a modest AI validation component, but it has no direct relevance to human reproductive medicine or to the reader's clinical AI focus.

scored.title: Structural Heart Interventions in Women with Congenital Heart Disease.
scored.why: This is a review article on transcatheter structural heart interventions in women with congenital heart disease, focused on sex-specific considerations in diagnosis and management, mentioning artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning only briefly as future tools for risk stratification. There is no primary data, algorithm, or evaluation presented, making this largely off-topic for the AI-focused beats despite its women's health framing.

scored.title: A Two-Stage Hybrid Feature Selection and Ensemble Learning Framework With Explainable AI for Accurate PCOS Prediction.
scored.why: This retrospective study built a hybrid XGBoost (a gradient-boosted decision tree algorithm) and multi-layer perceptron (MLP, a type of neural network) ensemble to classify polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) from clinical features, reporting 96.33% accuracy after SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) resampling and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)/LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) interpretability analysis. It uses a single dataset with no external validation or prospective testing, so it adds little beyond the many similar PCOS classifiers already published.

scored.title: Structure-Aware Deep Learning for Pediatric Echocardiographic Standard-View Classification in Ultrasonic Imaging.
scored.why: This study introduced PVTv2-ASEF, a structure-aware deep learning framework for classifying pediatric echocardiographic standard views, reporting modest macro-F1 improvements over a baseline transformer model on a private dataset and a small fetal ultrasound benchmark. The gains are incremental benchmark improvements with no prospective clinical evaluation or patient outcome data, and the work is not centered on reproductive medicine despite touching a fetal imaging dataset.

scored.title: MSCT-Trans: A Multi-scale Convolutional Neural Network Token Transformer for Interpretable Ultrasound Image Classification.
scored.why: This study proposed MSCT-Trans, a hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN) and transformer architecture for general-purpose ultrasound image classification, evaluated on breast, thyroid, and fetal imaging benchmarks with improved accuracy, macro-F1, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) compared with baseline models, plus interpretability analysis via Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping. The work is a benchmark-focused architecture paper without prospective clinical validation or a defined clinical endpoint, making it a routine incremental technical contribution for this reader's beats.

scored.title: Fetal brain MRI analysis: Towards clinical translation and impact.
scored.why: This narrative review summarizes advances in deep learning for fetal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), covering acquisition planning, segmentation, biometry, and quality control, and discusses barriers to clinical translation. As a review with no new data or evaluation, it offers useful orientation but does not meet the bar of a substantive finding this reader has not likely already encountered.

scored.title: Combining Statistical Modeling and Machine Learning for Prognostic Feature Selection in Cervical Cancer: A Retrospective Study Based on SEER 2004 to 2015 Data.
scored.why: This retrospective population-based study analyzed 5,392 cervical squamous cell carcinoma patients from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, combining logistic regression and machine learning to identify prognostic sociodemographic and clinical features, achieving a modest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.70. The machine learning component is used mainly for feature selection rather than as a deployable clinical tool, and the discrimination achieved is weak, limiting its practical impact.

scored.title: Evaluating large language models in patient education: a comparative analysis addressing frequently asked questions in peri-acetabular osteotomy.
scored.why: A single-center study had three surgeons blindly rate ChatGPT versus Google Gemini responses to ten common patient questions about peri-acetabular osteotomy (PAO) on a 5-point Likert scale, finding ChatGPT scored higher (4.17 vs 3.13) with similarly difficult readability for both. This is a small, non-clinician-comparator rubric evaluation of two chatbots against each other rather than against real clinicians or patients, making it routine for this beat.

scored.title: Nursing students' critical engagement with generative AI in evidence-based practice education: A qualitative descriptive study.
scored.why: This qualitative descriptive study analyzed 497 nursing student assessment submissions comparing their own evidence-based summaries to generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) outputs, identifying themes around credibility, critical thinking, and professional identity formation. It is an education-focused qualitative analysis with no patient-facing communication component and no clinician-comparator design, placing it at the margins of this beat.

scored.title: Artificial intelligence responses to toilet training questions: A reliability and readability analysis of ChatGPT and gemini applications.
scored.why: Five child development experts rated ChatGPT-4 Turbo and Gemini 2.0 Flash answers to ten toilet-training questions on a four-point Likert scale, finding Gemini scored slightly better on select items while producing more complex text by Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level. This is another small rubric-based chatbot comparison without a clinician-generated comparator or deployment, typical of routine output for this beat.

scored.title: Performance of Large Language Models in Oral Cancer Patient Education: An Evaluation of Reliability, Readability, and Patient Communication Quality.
scored.why: Four large language models (LLMs) were evaluated on 22 oral cancer patient questions using standardized reliability instruments (DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA, GQS) and six readability indices, finding significant differences in reliability scores and that all models exceeded recommended sixth-grade readability. This is a routine rubric-based, no-clinician-comparator evaluation typical of the high-volume, low-novelty studies in this beat.

scored.title: Artificial intelligence chatbots as information sources for postherpetic neuralgia: An evaluation of reliability and readability.
scored.why: Four AI chatbots were tested on 11 postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) queries using DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA, and Global Quality Scale (GQS) instruments plus six readability indices, finding moderate quality differences and that none met the recommended sixth-grade reading level. This is another routine rubric-only chatbot evaluation without any clinician comparator, deployment, or measured patient effect.

scored.title: Precision Education: How Ready Are Obstetrics and Gynecology Clerkships for the Future of Medical Education?
scored.why: This is a survey of obstetrics and gynecology clerkship directors assessing adoption of 'precision education' tools, including limited use of artificial intelligence teaching assistants (6%) and augmented reality (17%), with no clinical AI system evaluated. It offers a snapshot of medical education infrastructure rather than any finding about AI performance or patient outcomes relevant to this reader's beats.

scored.title: Predictive design of tissue-specific mammalian enhancers that function in the mouse embryo.
scored.why: This study used deep learning, specifically convolutional neural networks trained on chromatin accessibility data and fine-tuned by transfer learning, to design synthetic tissue-specific enhancers that were validated as functional in mouse embryos. It is an impressive genomics and synthetic biology result but has no clinical AI, reproductive medicine, or patient-facing component relevant to this reader's beats.

scored.title: Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis and Machine Learning Reveal that USP1 Drives Lipid Metabolism and Macrophage Polarization in Cervical Cancer Cells.
scored.why: This laboratory study used weighted gene co-expression network analysis and three machine learning algorithms (LASSO, support vector machine recursive feature elimination, and random forest) merely as a feature-selection step to identify USP1 as a hub gene, then conducted wet-lab experiments on cervical cancer cell lines and a mouse xenograft model. The core contribution is molecular biology and mechanism, not an AI or clinical decision tool, so it falls outside the scope of clinical AI or reproductive AI beats despite touching cervical cancer.

scored.title: Reading Level Is Not Comprehension: Rethinking How We Evaluate ChatGPT for Patient Education in Adult Spinal Deformity.
scored.why: This appears to be a commentary piece titled about rethinking how reading-level metrics are used to evaluate ChatGPT's patient education materials for adult spinal deformity, but no abstract or substantive content was provided. Without any described methodology, data, or findings, this cannot be scored as a meaningful research contribution.

scored.title: When Deepfakes Meet Herd Immunity: Artificial Intelligence, Vaccine Avoidance, and the Next Infodemic Threat.
scored.why: This is a perspective article arguing that generative artificial intelligence (AI), including deepfakes and chatbots, poses a growing infodemic risk to vaccine confidence and herd immunity, drawing on historical and epidemiological reasoning rather than presenting new data. It contains no study of a language model interacting with patients or any clinical AI evaluation, so it falls outside the scope of the LLM-patient-communication beat despite AI being discussed.

scored.title: Innovations in dementia education in health sciences: curriculum design and partnerships across three countries.
scored.why: This brief report descriptively summarizes dementia education innovations, including generative artificial intelligence-based simulation, presented at a 2025 academic plenary session across Canada, the United Kingdom, and Hong Kong. It contains no evaluation of an AI system's performance or effect on patients or learners, functioning as a conference summary rather than original research relevant to this reader's beats.

scored.title: A clinician-centered evaluation framework for large language models in patient education: Integrating the Technology Acceptance Model and Medical Condition Regard Scale.
scored.why: This is a Viewpoint proposing a new theoretical evaluation framework, the Technology Acceptance Model paired with the Medical Condition Regard Scale (TAM-MCRS), for rating large language model (LLM)-generated patient education, but it presents no actual data, comparison, or deployment. As an opinion and framework piece with no empirical findings, it offers little of substance for this beat this week.

scored.title: A rubric to assess generative AI-based feedback on student writing assignments.
scored.why: This paper describes a rubric developed to help instructors compare generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) feedback tools on undergraduate science writing assignments across five criteria like accuracy and constructiveness. It concerns classroom writing feedback with no patient communication component whatsoever, placing it outside the scope of this beat.
